title: Experiment Runway: Cadence, Automated Eval Gates, and Rollback Thresholds
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable, low-friction 'experiment runway' that combines cadence, automated evaluation gates, and explicit rollback thresholds for feature experiments (A/B, traffic canaries, multi-model routing).

Scope: Deliver a prescriptive milestone cadence, a set of automated evaluation hooks (metric + qualitative probes), and CLI/Console guardrails for automatic/semiautomatic rollback. This ticket covers the PM-level acceptance criteria, evaluation signal definitions, and runbook handoffs to eng/ops. It does NOT cover the low-level kernel scheduling or batching optimizations used by the runtime (those are owned by ENG).

Why now: Multiple product teams have had partial regressions slip through canaries because we lacked standard cadence and automated evaluation thresholds for experiment health (see incidents: INC-2026-02-11 and postmortem notes). Aligning cadence + automated gates reduces risk while enabling faster rollouts to meet OKR: "Ship 12 high-confidence experiments per quarter".
milestones: M1: Define experiment cadence and milestone rubric (artifact: cadence-runbook v0.1) — target 2026-03-01
M2: Instrument automated eval hooks (latency/cost/quality/semantic drift) with clear thresholds — target 2026-03-15
M3: Console guardrail mockups + API spec for automatic rollback triggers — target 2026-03-22
M4: Pilot with Search team on two experiments (A/B and model fallback) — target 2026-03-29
M5: Post-pilot retros and iterate to v1 runway (handbook page + templates) — target 2026-04-04
acceptance_criteria: A1: A single-page 'Experiment Runway' runbook is published in Confluence with milestone cadence and decision matrix

A2: At least 3 automated eval hooks implemented and testable in staging: latency regression (>10ms per-token), quality regression (BLEU-like or eval set score drop >2%), cost delta (+15%), and error rate (>0.5% increase)
A3: Console exposes a checkbox and policy selector to enable automatic rollback and to set thresholds per-route/model
A4: Pilot experiments succeed in catching one injected regression (simulated) and trigger the rollback policy in staging
A5: Hand-off doc and checklist for product/engineering/ops included in the runbook
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Definition: PM + Eng + Design align on signals and cadence (2 weeks)
Phase 1 — Instrumentation: ENG builds eval hooks and exposes signals to Console/Telemetry (1 week)
Phase 2 — Guardrails: UX for threshold configuration + automatic rollback toggle (1 week)
Phase 3 — Pilot: Run 2 live experiments with Search and Composer teams; observe and adapt (1 week)
Phase 4 — Stabilize: Update runbook, add templates, teach via office hours (1 week)

2026-03-05 — Product review: Decided to favor automatic rollback for 'safety-net' signals (latency/error-rate) and semi-automatic (notify + manual abort) for quality signals that require human review.
2026-03-10 — Asha Kapoor: Pilot plan submitted; Search team agreed to run two short experiments with simulated regressions to validate gates. Added test matrix to Confluence.

notes: Tradeoffs called out: aggressive auto-rollback reduces blast radius but risks false positives on noisy quality metrics. We will start with conservative thresholds and rely on manual review for semantic drift signals until we have better eval coverage. Operational runbook includes templated post-rollback triage steps and Slack escalation playbook.
